facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer
facts.quote: Adobe Journey Optimizer is an enterprise application for creating and delivering connected, contextual, and personalized customer experiences across all channels and touchpoints. It is built natively on Adobe Experience Platform and leverages a unified real-time customer profile, an API-first open framework, centralized offer decisioning, and AI/ML capabilities.
facts.supports: Adobe's definition of Journey Optimizer, and that it is built on Adobe Experience Platform and its real-time customer profile.

facts.title: Experience League: Understanding Journey Optimizer
facts.quote: Automates real-time, multi-step sequences of interactions (journeys) or sends a scheduled or API-triggered message to an audience (campaigns).
facts.supports: What a journey is and what a campaign is in Journey Optimizer.

facts.title: Experience League: Understanding Journey Optimizer
facts.quote: Delivers messages through channels like email, mobile messages, push notifications, and direct mail, and exports data to external systems.
facts.supports: The channels Journey Optimizer delivers messages through.

facts.title: Experience League: Understanding Journey Optimizer
facts.quote: Tracks customer engagement and campaign performance with reports for continuous improvement.
facts.supports: Journey Optimizer reports on customer engagement and campaign performance.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Get Started for System Admin
facts.quote: The Administrator sets up the environment first. Data engineers, developers, and marketers depend on this work being complete before they can begin.
facts.supports: Adobe's implementation order starts with the administrator's environment setup.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Get Started for System Admin
facts.quote: Plan at least one development sandbox for building and testing, and one production sandbox for sending to customers. Channel configurations are also set up per sandbox, so messages cannot be sent from a sandbox until you configure them there.
facts.supports: A development and a production sandbox, each with its own channel configurations.

facts.title: Experience League: Create your first journey
facts.quote: Test your journey with test profiles before activation
facts.supports: Journeys are tested with test profiles before they are activated.

facts.title: Experience League: Updated reporting experience
facts.quote: This seamless integration between Journey Optimizer and Customer Journey Analytics provides a clearer view of performance metrics, enabling users to make more informed decisions.
facts.supports: Journey Optimizer reporting is integrated with Customer Journey Analytics.

facts.title: Experience League: Manage opt-out
facts.quote: When sending messages from journeys or campaigns, you must always ensure that customers can unsubscribe from future communications. Once unsubscribed, the profiles are automatically removed from the audience of future marketing messages.
facts.supports: Unsubscribes must be offered, and unsubscribed profiles are removed from future marketing audiences automatically.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Get Started for System Admin
facts.quote: Apply access labels to objects like journeys, campaigns, and channel configurations to control which users can access specific resources.
facts.supports: Object-level access control with access labels.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer
facts.quote: Components and capabilities available in your environment depend on your permissions and on your licensing package
facts.supports: What a client can use depends on their licensing package.

facts.title: Experience League: Updated reporting experience
facts.quote: Reporting in Adobe Journey Optimizer is currently standardized to UTC.
facts.supports: Reports are in UTC only.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Get Started for System Admin
facts.quote: When accessing Journey Optimizer for the first time, you are provisioned a production sandbox and allocated a certain number of IPs depending on your contract.
facts.supports: Sending IPs depend on the contract.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Overview
facts.quote: With Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, you can orchestrate person and account journeys using built-in generative AI and industry-leading automation to maximize demand for specific offerings using marketing-qualified buying groups.
facts.supports: Adobe's one-sentence description of Journey Optimizer B2B Edition.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Overview
facts.quote: the key distinction is that account journeys move accounts through the journey, not people
facts.supports: Account journeys move accounts, not individual people.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Overview
facts.quote: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition is built on Adobe Experience Platform, including Real-Time CDP B2B. Journey Optimizer B2B Edition and Marketo Engage run on separate systems, each with its own data store. Experience Platform is the primary data store and authoritative source for accounts, people, and opportunities. Journey Optimizer B2B Edition owns your account journeys, buying groups, and buying group roles.
facts.supports: The architecture: built on Experience Platform with Real-Time CDP B2B, which holds accounts, people and opportunities; the B2B Edition holds account journeys and buying groups.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Overview
facts.quote: A dedicated Marketo Engage instance supports each Journey Optimizer B2B Edition subscription. This instance does not store your account journeys, audiences, or buying groups. Instead, it provides entitlements and backend services, such as email delivery, sender configuration, and branding domains. To support journey actions, you can also connect one or more of your existing Marketo Engage instances, including your production instance. Journey actions let marketers coordinate account-based journeys in Journey Optimizer B2B Edition with lead-based campaigns in Marketo Engage, such as adding people to a list or a request campaign.
facts.supports: A dedicated Marketo Engage instance provides backend services such as email delivery, and existing Marketo Engage instances can be connected so journeys can add people to Marketo lists and request campaigns.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Overview
facts.quote: Marketers implement the journey by splitting paths using account criteria, people criteria, or buying group criteria. On each path, actions send communications or wait for an event to occur.
facts.supports: How an account journey is built: split paths and actions.

facts.title: Experience League: Buying Groups
facts.quote: Within the account, there could be a subset of people who comprise the buying group
facts.supports: A buying group is a subset of the people in an account.

facts.title: Experience League: Buying Groups
facts.quote: These people ultimately make the purchase decision, so they need special attention from the marketer and might need different information delivered to them than the other people associated with the account.
facts.supports: What a buying group is: the people in an account who make the purchase decision.

facts.title: Experience League: Intelligent Dashboard
facts.quote: The Intelligent Dashboard provides a comprehensive view of buying group and account metrics, helping you to monitor and strategize your marketing efforts more effectively.
facts.supports: The Intelligent Dashboard reports buying group and account metrics.

facts.title: Experience League: Setup checklist
facts.quote: To send emails from Journey Optimizer B2B Edition, configure the email tracking and deliverability in the attached Marketo Engage production instance and in the Journey Optimizer B2B Edition app.
facts.supports: Email tracking and deliverability are configured in the attached Marketo Engage instance and in the B2B Edition app.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Overview
facts.quote: Use Real-Time CDP account segmentation to build and evaluate the account audiences and people audiences that qualify accounts and people for a journey.
facts.supports: Audiences for a journey are built with Real-Time CDP account segmentation.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Overview
facts.quote: Qualifying accounts enter a published journey within 24 hours.
facts.supports: Accounts do not enter a journey instantly.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Journey Optimizer B2B Edition Overview
facts.quote: Account journeys do not appear in Marketo Engage, and they are only usable in Journey Optimizer B2B Edition.
facts.supports: Account journeys are not visible in Marketo Engage.

facts.title: Experience League: Intelligent Dashboard
facts.quote: Intent data is included when it is configured for your Journey Optimizer B2B Edition instance.
facts.supports: Intent detection needs intent data to be configured.

facts.title: Experience League: Activate Marketo Engage to Support Journey Actions
facts.quote: A journey action does not create a new person record in Marketo Engage when a matching record does not exist.
facts.supports: Marketo journey actions only act on people who already exist in Marketo Engage.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
facts.quote: By integrating with Adobe Target and Adobe Journey Optimizer, it provides a centralized platform for managing, analyzing, and optimizing experiments.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of what Experimentation Accelerator is.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
facts.quote: The Experiments tab centralizes the tracking and analysis of tests from Adobe Journey Optimizer and Adobe Target. You can view all experiments, review KPIs, and filter or search to locate specific tests.
facts.supports: One list of experiments from Journey Optimizer and Target, with KPIs.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
facts.quote: identifies the treatment currently delivering the best performance.
facts.supports: The Current Leader metric on an experiment.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
facts.quote: measures the percentage improvement of the leading treatment compared to the control or baseline.
facts.supports: The Lift Over Baseline metric on an experiment.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
facts.quote: The Hypothesis captures the planned changes to be tested and documents the expected impact on the primary metric.
facts.supports: What the hypothesis on an experiment records.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
facts.quote: The Opportunities panel displays AI-generated recommendations designed to enhance test performance and align with broader business objectives and KPIs.
facts.supports: The Opportunities panel recommends what to test.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
facts.quote: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator only makes recommendations of what could be changed and how it could be changed. Only users who have permissions to change the experience using Journey Optimizer or Target will be able to act on these recommendations. All recommendations can be reviewed and edited before being pushed out.
facts.supports: Experimentation Accelerator recommends only; people with permission act on the recommendations after review.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
facts.quote: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator only ingests and analyzes data, producing insights and recommendations for future testing. It does not have access to modify any test settings.
facts.supports: It cannot modify test settings.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
facts.quote: A dedicated model is trained for every sandbox. When a sandbox is deleted, all related data, signals, and models are permanently removed.
facts.supports: One model per sandbox.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
facts.quote: We only use customer data to train or fine-tune the model from that customer.
facts.supports: A customer's data trains only that customer's model.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
facts.quote: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator requires a paid license for customers and integrates seamlessly with either Adobe Target or Adobe Journey Optimizer.
facts.supports: Experimentation Accelerator is licensed separately.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
facts.quote: Opportunities feature is limited to experiments with text-based changes.
facts.supports: Opportunities are only generated for text-based changes.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator monitor
facts.quote: If your organization uses only Adobe Target as the reporting source, you cannot change the primary metric after the test is published.
facts.supports: The primary metric cannot be changed where Target is the only reporting source.

facts.title: Experience League: Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator
facts.quote: Any A/B activities in Target appear in Journey Optimizer Experimentation Accelerator in the production sandbox of Journey Optimizer.
facts.supports: Only Target's A/B activities are brought in.

facts.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Overview
facts.quote: Content Analytics helps marketers to understand how content impacts the key performance indicators that a business has defined.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of what Content Analytics is for.

facts.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Overview
facts.quote: Content Analytics uses an AI and machine learning based featurization service to break content down into components and attributes. By creating a structured metadata profile on all your content, you can analyze what content and what attributes of that content drive business results.
facts.supports: How it works: content is broken down into components and attributes so they can be analyzed against results.

facts.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Overview
facts.quote: the Experience Platform Web or Mobile SDK records impressions and interactions with the content.
facts.supports: The Web or Mobile SDK records content impressions and interactions.

facts.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Overview
facts.quote: You can use the Content Analytics data, together with behavioral data and other lookup data, in a Customer Journey Analytics setup
facts.supports: Content Analytics data is used inside Customer Journey Analytics.

facts.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Reporting
facts.quote: A specific Workspace template is available, so you can immediately access a pre-populated Workspace project with relevant content insights.
facts.supports: A ready-made Workspace template for content reporting.

facts.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Overview
facts.quote: With Content Analytics you get insights on which assets are receiving impressions and where assets are receiving impressions.
facts.supports: Content usage insights.

facts.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Overview
facts.quote: Content Analytics can provide engagement insights like the average click through rate for assets with certain attributes.
facts.supports: Content engagement insights.

facts.title: Experience League: Configure Content Analytics
facts.quote: Use the Content Analytics guided configuration wizard to guide you through all steps required to set up the prerequisites for a configuration of Content Analytics.
facts.supports: The guided configuration wizard takes you through the setup.

facts.title: Experience League: Configure Content Analytics
facts.quote: Only when you manually publish the Tags property is your Content Analytics configuration effectively deployed and data collection started.
facts.supports: Data collection starts when the Tags property is published.

facts.title: Experience League: Configure Content Analytics
facts.quote: To provide a user or group of users access to Content Analytics, you must provide the user or group of users access to one or more data views that are configured for Content Analytics
facts.supports: Access is given through data views.

facts.title: Experience League: Configure Content Analytics
facts.quote: The text content seen by any given user can be reproduced using the page URL and does not depend on cookies or other personalization mechanisms.
facts.supports: Experience reporting needs pages whose text does not vary by visitor.

facts.title: Experience League: Configure Content Analytics
facts.quote: You have allow-listed the User Agent and IP address for the featurization service that is used in Content Analytics.
facts.supports: The client's site must let Adobe's featurization service in.

facts.title: Experience League: Configure Content Analytics
facts.quote: There is no Content Analytics permission that you can configure to enable or disable Content Analytics access for individual users or groups of users.
facts.supports: There is no separate Content Analytics permission.

facts.title: Experience League: Content Analytics Overview
facts.quote: That process consists of a retrieval service that revisits the public-facing versions of the configured URLs that define the interactions and the HTML that defines the experience.
facts.supports: Adobe's service reads the public-facing pages.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics overview
facts.quote: Marketing Campaign Analytics, powered by Adobe Sensei, enables marketers to measure campaigns and optimize planning holistically across all channels: paid, earned, and owned.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of Marketing Campaign Analytics.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics overview
facts.quote: Marketing Campaign Analytics provides the incremental impact of all marketing activities on business and campaign outcomes through a holistic (end-to-end) measurement application for digital and offline marketing.
facts.supports: It measures the incremental impact of marketing, digital and offline.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics overview
facts.quote: The AI/ML bi-directional transfer learning unifies marketing mix modeling (MMM) and multi-touch attribution (MTA) results to ensure consistent results across measurement and planning in a cookie-less world.
facts.supports: Marketing mix modeling and multi-touch attribution are unified by transfer learning.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics overview
facts.quote: Marketing mix modeling in Marketing Campaign Analytics is a privacy-friendly machine learning analysis used to measure the incremental impact of various marketing tactics and business factors on conversion metrics.
facts.supports: What marketing mix modeling is in this product.

facts.title: Experience League: Ingest data overview
facts.quote: Marketing Campaign Analytics works with event level data, aggregate or summary marketing effort data from various walled gardens. And with aggregate or summary data from any other source, like offline advertising, internal factors or external factors.
facts.supports: The kinds of data it works with.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics workflow
facts.quote: Configure mapping rules and conflict resolution rules to merge the various marketing datasets needed to measure and plan campaign performance in Marketing Campaign Analytics.
facts.supports: The harmonize step of Adobe's workflow.

facts.title: Experience League: Models Overview
facts.quote: A model in Marketing Campaign Analytics is a machine learning model employed to measure and predict a specified outcome based on marketing investments.
facts.supports: What a model is.

facts.title: Experience League: Plans overview
facts.quote: Plans in Marketing Campaign Analytics allow you to allocate budgets by business unit and channel. The planning functionality is integrated with the outcomes of the trained models based on your harmonized data.
facts.supports: Plans allocate budgets from the trained models.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics overview
facts.quote: Develop multiple budget plans and compare their impact to make optimal decisions for your business.
facts.supports: Budget scenarios can be compared.

facts.title: Experience League: Access controls
facts.quote: Access control for Marketing Campaign Analytics is provided through Experience Platform in the Adobe Admin Console and through Permissions in Experience Platform.
facts.supports: How access is controlled.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Campaign Analytics overview
facts.quote: Multi-touch attribution cannot measure most offline touchpoints such as print ads, billboards, or TV commercials and business factors.
facts.supports: Multi-touch attribution does not cover most offline touchpoints.

facts.title: Experience League: Plans overview
facts.quote: If a model that you have used for your plan is scored on new data, you need to create a new plan to take into account the rescored data.
facts.supports: A plan does not update itself when the model is rescored.

facts.title: Experience League: Models Overview
facts.quote: Also, when data is added to the model, a manual rescore of the model is required.
facts.supports: Rescoring is manual.

facts.title: Experience League: Plans overview
facts.quote: Some of the Experience League content might still refer to Mix Modeler instead of Marketing Campaign Analytics.
facts.supports: Adobe's pages still use the older product name in places.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview
facts.quote: With Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration, you can discover, activate, and measure high-value audiences without relying on third-party cookies. This solution enables advanced data collaborations, helping you create personalized and impactful customer experiences in a privacy-centric, centralized environment.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of Real-Time CDP Collaboration.

facts.title: Experience League: Use cases in Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration
facts.quote: Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration enables collaboration with advertisers and publishers, unlocking new opportunities for audience discovery, activation, and measurement.
facts.supports: It is for collaboration between advertisers and publishers.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview
facts.quote: Collaborators can form connections in a privacy-centric environment to match audiences, discover potential new customers, and maximize ad return on available inventory.
facts.supports: Collaborators connect to match audiences.

facts.title: Experience League: Collaborate overview
facts.quote: Projects are the heart of Real-Time CDP Collaboration, enabling you to run audience overlap calculations, discover relevant audiences, activate audiences in your advertising platforms, and measure campaign performance.
facts.supports: What a project does.

facts.title: Experience League: Use cases in Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration
facts.quote: Get insight into overlap percentages and the number of overlapping identities between your audiences and those of your collaborators.
facts.supports: The overlap insight in the Discover use case.

facts.title: Experience League: Use cases in Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration
facts.quote: View campaign performance in simplified and customizable reports.
facts.supports: The Measure use case reports campaign performance.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview
facts.quote: Embedded controls ensure that governance and privacy requirements are met, guiding the responsible use of audience data at every step of your workflows.
facts.supports: Governance and privacy controls are built in.

facts.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration Quick Start & Setup Guide
facts.quote: Your organization's access roles determine what users can see and do in Collaboration.
facts.supports: Setup starts with role-based access.

facts.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration Quick Start & Setup Guide
facts.quote: Define your account's role in Collaboration, provide branding assets, and configure match keys to align audiences across connections.
facts.supports: The account setup: role, branding assets and match keys.

facts.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration Quick Start & Setup Guide
facts.quote: Determine which profiles are eligible to be included in connections by selecting a consent mode: opt-in, opt-out, or none.
facts.supports: A consent mode decides which profiles can be included.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview
facts.quote: Adobe Real-Time Customer Data Platform (CDP) Collaboration is currently available in the United States, Canada, Australia, New Zealand, and across Europe, the Middle East, and Africa
facts.supports: The regions the product is offered in.

facts.title: Experience League: Collaborate overview
facts.quote: Currently, the only available advertising platform in Real-Time CDP Collaboration is Amazon Marketing Cloud (AMC).
facts.supports: Only one advertising platform is available.

facts.title: Experience League: Overview
facts.quote: Note that some of the measurement automation is not available in the first release.
facts.supports: Measurement automation is partial.

facts.title: Experience League: Use cases in Adobe Real-Time CDP Collaboration
facts.quote: To set up a cloud data warehouse destination, please contact your Adobe representative.
facts.supports: Cloud data warehouse destinations are set up through Adobe.

facts.title: Experience League: Real-Time CDP Collaboration Quick Start & Setup Guide
facts.quote: Advertisers can source up to 25 audiences.
facts.supports: A limit on sourced audiences.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Analytics overview
facts.quote: Adobe Analytics enables organizations to gather data and gain actionable insights from any digital customer interaction. With in-depth analysis, versatile reporting, and predictive intelligence, organizations get the insightful foundation they need to build better experiences for their customers.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of Adobe Analytics.

facts.title: Experience League: Analysis Workspace Overview
facts.quote: Analysis Workspace allows you to build analyses quickly to gather insights and then share those insights with others. Using the drag-and-drop browser interface, you can craft your analysis, add visualizations to bring data to life, curate a dataset, and share and schedule projects with anyone you choose.
facts.supports: What Analysis Workspace does.

facts.title: Experience League: Implement Adobe Analytics
facts.quote: Adobe Analytics requires code within your website, mobile app, or other application to send data to data collection servers.
facts.supports: Adobe Analytics needs code on the site or app.

facts.title: Experience League: Implement Adobe Analytics
facts.quote: The standardized and recommended method to implement Adobe Analytics for new customers. Add the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK extension in Adobe Experience Platform Data Collection
facts.supports: The Web SDK extension is Adobe's recommended method for new customers.

facts.title: Experience League: Create a solution design document
facts.quote: A solution design document (also known as a solution design reference or business requirements document) is in essence the blueprint of your analytics implementation. It defines criteria identified by stakeholders throughout your organization, and translates them to variables within Adobe Analytics.
facts.supports: What a solution design document is.

facts.title: Experience League: Implement Adobe Analytics using the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK
facts.quote: You can use the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK to send data to Adobe Analytics.
facts.supports: The Web SDK sends data to Adobe Analytics.

facts.title: Experience League: Product profiles for Adobe Analytics
facts.quote: Product profiles are permission presets that product admins can assign to users within an organization.
facts.supports: What a product profile is.

facts.title: Experience League: Product profiles for Adobe Analytics
facts.quote: A user must belong to at least one report suite to be given access to use Adobe Analytics.
facts.supports: Access depends on report suites.

facts.title: Experience League: Analytics Data Feed Overview
facts.quote: Data feeds are a powerful way to get raw data out of Adobe Analytics. This raw data can be used in other platforms outside of Adobe to use at your organization's discretion. Data is delivered in hourly batches at the conclusion of each hour, or in daily batches at the conclusion of each day.
facts.supports: Data feeds deliver raw data in hourly or daily batches.

facts.title: Experience League: Analytics Integration
facts.quote: A4T integrates Adobe Analytics and Adobe Target together.
facts.supports: The Analytics for Target integration.

facts.title: Experience League: Implement Adobe Analytics using the Adobe Experience Platform Web SDK
facts.quote: If your organization requires a new Web SDK implementation and plans to use Customer Journey Analytics in the future, Adobe recommends a clean Web SDK implementation using your own schema.
facts.supports: Adobe's advice where Customer Journey Analytics is planned.

facts.title: Experience League: Analytics Data Feed Overview
facts.quote: A bucket configured on Amazon S3, Google Cloud Platform, Azure RBAC, or Azure SAS.
facts.supports: A data feed needs a cloud storage bucket.

facts.title: Experience League: Adobe Analytics overview
facts.quote: Customer Journey Analytics is Adobe's next-generation Analytics solution that lets you use the power of Analysis Workspace with data from Adobe Experience Platform.
facts.supports: Adobe positions Customer Journey Analytics as the next generation.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Attribution
facts.quote: Marketo Measure gives marketers insight into which marketing efforts are the most effective in driving revenue for their company. Marketo Measure is a marketing attribution solution that automatically tracks and reports on channel performance, providing visibility into which channels are driving the most customer engagement and allowing you to optimize your marketing spend accordingly.
facts.supports: Adobe's description of Marketo Measure.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketing Attribution
facts.quote: Marketing attribution is the process of assigning revenue credit to a marketing touchpoint. This is done by tracking a prospect's entire customer journey, starting from their first interaction with your company to when the deal closes.
facts.supports: What marketing attribution is.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketo Measure Attribution Models
facts.quote: Marketo Measure offers six types of attribution models:
facts.supports: The number of attribution models.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketo Measure Attribution Models
facts.quote: First Touch and Lead Creation are simple, single-touch models. The remaining four are more complex, multi-touch models.
facts.supports: Single-touch and multi-touch models.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketo Measure Framework
facts.quote: The Marketo Measure JavaScript tracks all the online marketing interactions, also called touchpoints, that prospects/leads have with your organization.
facts.supports: The JavaScript tracks online touchpoints.

facts.title: Experience League: Adding Marketo Measure Script
facts.quote: Marketo Measure JavaScript that you'd like tracked by Marketo Measure should be added to all web properties as soon as possible. Once the JavaScript is deployed, Marketo Measure starts collecting your digital data.
facts.supports: The script goes on all web properties.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketo Measure Framework
facts.quote: Marketo Measure integrates with CRMs to house and organize all the data that is captured by the Marketo Measure JS.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketo Measure CRM Packageless Integration
facts.quote: Through the standard Marketo Measure installation, you are required to install a Salesforce Package or a Microsoft Dynamics Managed Solution.
facts.supports: The standard installation puts a package in the CRM.

facts.title: Experience League: ROI Dashboard
facts.quote: The ROI Dashboard provides marketers with a granular view of returns on investment across channels, subchannels, and campaigns.
facts.supports: The ROI Dashboard.

facts.title: Experience League: Spend Management Methods
facts.quote: Spend data is key to the success of ROI reporting with Marketo Measure. To have accurate and comprehensive ROI reporting across all of your channels and subchannels, you must make sure you have the appropriate spend data being pulled into Marketo Measure.
facts.supports: ROI reporting depends on spend data.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketo Measure Ultimate Implementation Guide
facts.quote: The direct CRM and Marketo Engage connections are no longer available for Ultimate.
facts.supports: Marketo Measure Ultimate brings data in through Experience Platform instead.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketo Measure Ultimate Implementation Guide
facts.quote: Ultimate does not push data back to the CRM. Customers can consume data from the data warehouse.
facts.supports: Ultimate does not write to the CRM.

facts.title: Experience League: Marketo Measure Cookies
facts.quote: Adobe is deprecating Marketo Measure functions which rely on third-party cookies; specifically, Cross-Domain Tracking and View-through Attribution
facts.supports: Two functions that relied on third-party cookies are deprecated.

facts.title: Experience League: Integrated Ad Platforms
facts.quote: Marketo Measure has API connections with Google AdWords, Microsoft BingAds, Facebook Ads and DoubleClick Campaign Manager.
